This is actually a very real lineage now. What you’re circling is not fantasy — it’s an emerging hybrid between:

venture studio

holding company

cultural/media ecosystem

micro-PE

patronage network

founder collective

taste institution

But your version is more culturally intelligent and less financially extractive than most of the current examples.

Here’s the examples list I’d honestly build around for Understudy research:

Foundational Holding Companies / Long-Term Ownership

Tiny
Probably the single most important reference point for you. Started by buying small internet businesses and evolved into a long-term holdco model. Quiet, taste-driven, founder-friendly, anti-hypergrowth in tone. 

Permanent Equity
Long-hold private equity focused on sane ownership and operational continuity instead of rapid exits. Philosophically very close to “non-reactive companies.”

Chenmark
Quiet long-term acquirer of small/medium businesses. Very operationally grounded. Strong example of “boring but durable.”

Enduring Ventures
Permanent holding company style investing in profitable small companies rather than hype startups. 

Venture Studios / Company Builders

Idealab
One of the original venture studios. Created over 150 companies. Important historically because it showed that parallel company creation can work. 

Betaworks
One of the smartest references for Understudy. Hybrid of media, software, internet culture, and incubation. Invested in weird internet-native ideas early.

Expa
Founder-focused studio/incubator model. More polished Silicon Valley version.

25madison
Interesting because they focus on overlooked “archaic markets” and operational modernization. Very aligned with your instincts around fragmented industries. 

High Alpha
Studio model specifically for SaaS companies. Good operational example.

Cultural / Taste / Media Ecosystem Companies

A24
Maybe the most important modern taste company. Not just films — atmosphere, identity, audience trust, cultural coherence. Eventually became a distribution and identity engine, not merely a production company. 

Annapurna Pictures
Interesting hybrid of art-film patronage + gaming + media infrastructure. 

Monocle
One of the clearest examples of media becoming:

commerce

hospitality

worldview

retail

travel

taste infrastructure

Extremely important reference for Understudy media strategy.

NTS Radio
Built cultural authority first, then ecosystem power.

Are.na
Tiny but hugely influential in creative/intellectual circles. Great example of slow thoughtful internet culture.

Fan / Community Ownership Models

Legion M
Very interesting because they experimented with community-owned media production. 

Calm / Alternative Capital Models

Calm Company Fund
Extremely relevant philosophically. Explicitly anti-“grow at all costs.”

Basecamp
Not a holdco, but hugely important culturally:

calm software

anti-hustle

profitable

opinionated

operationally sane

Understudy could honestly become:
“Basecamp philosophy applied to investing and company creation.”

Most Important Insight From The Research

The successful versions of these models all eventually became:

trust networks

taste filters

founder magnets

cultural institutions

NOT merely investment firms.

That’s the real pattern.

A24 is not just movies.
Tiny is not just acquisitions.
Monocle is not just a magazine.
Betaworks is not just a venture studio.

They became:
curators of a worldview.

That’s the level Understudy should probably think on.

And honestly the strongest unique angle you have is:
combining:

humane systems

AI

operational durability

media/culture

physical businesses

emotional/environmental intelligence

small-scale entrepreneurship

I don’t actually see many firms coherently combining all those layers yet.


And what companies have these guys invested in when they were super small weird one guy a future Virgil ablow nerd video game maker etc

This is the exact lineage you should study.

Not “traditional startups.”

More like:

strange talented people

tiny weird projects

obsessive builders

culturally intelligent founders

people institutions ignored early

Because that’s where asymmetry lives.

Some especially important examples for Understudy:

Figma
Dylan Field was basically a design nerd kid with a strange conviction that browser-based collaborative design tools mattered before most people understood the category. Early versions took YEARS and almost looked like failures. 

Cursor
One of the clearest modern examples. Backed absurdly early by Neo because Ali Partovi specifically hunts elite weird technical people before institutions fully see them. 

Gumroad
Sahil Lavingia accidentally became one of the prototypes for the “calm profitable internet company.” It survived because it embraced sustainability over hypergrowth after VC pressure almost killed it. 

Nomad List
Pieter Levels is hugely important to your thinking whether you realize it or not. One weird guy building internet-native utilities with tiny teams and strong personal worldview. He basically helped invent modern indie hacking culture. 

PhotoAI
Also Pieter Levels. Tiny team. Fast iteration. Personal internet distribution instead of institutional scaling. 

TypingMind
This is VERY relevant to Tilth. It was essentially “better UI for ChatGPT” made by indie hackers before large companies optimized the experience. 

Product Hunt
Started from internet/product community culture. Ryan Hoover later created Weekend Fund specifically because networks of weird builders became deal flow. 

A24
Not a startup in the normal sense. Important because they proved that:
taste itself can become infrastructure.

That’s crucial for Understudy.

Monocle
Magazine → retail → radio → hospitality → worldview ecosystem. Another example of “taste as operating system.”

Are.na
Tiny, weird, highly influential. Built around intellectual and creative workflows rather than engagement addiction.

NTS Radio
Started as niche cultural infrastructure and became globally influential because it preserved trust and curation.

Betaworks
Probably one of the strongest Understudy references structurally. They invested in strange internet-native ideas very early and treated internet culture as signal. They backed things like:

Giphy

Tumblr ecosystem companies

media tools

creator tools

weird internet products

Some investors themselves matter as examples:

Cyan Banister
One of the most important examples for you psychologically. She specifically became famous for investing in “magically weird” founders and strange early projects before mainstream validation. Early investor in:

Uber

SpaceX

Postmates

Affirm

Opendoor

Ali Partovi
Another huge example. He invested absurdly early in:

Facebook

Airbnb

Dropbox

Uber
and later created Neo to identify strange brilliant technical young people early.
